canonical_name: Samsung Bioepis / Epis NexLab – G2GBio (GB-7001, InnoLAMP™)

current_status.stage: Research collaboration & license agreement signed (March 2026); preclinical
current_status.partner: Samsung Bioepis / Epis NexLab (full license on long-acting semaglutide asset + option on a 2nd asset + first-negotiation rights on 3 more undisclosed assets); Boehringer Ingelheim (separate LAI peptide formulation collaboration since Jan 2025, expanded July 2026); Celltrion (MOU for InnoBioLAMP antibody SC platform)
current_status.data_point: InnoLAMP: <5% initial drug burst in first 24h; serum concentrations maintained beyond 28 days in rodent models across semaglutide, tirzepatide, and retatrutide

finding_history.summary: G2GBio debuted on KOSDAQ (ticker 456160) with IPO priced at the top of the range (₩58,000/share, ₩52.2B raised), drawing 810.6:1 institutional demand. Shares closed the first trading day up 61.7% at ₩93,800 (intraday high +69.3% at ₩98,200), giving a ₩503.3B market cap. Independently corroborated by a second outlet reporting a ~60% first-day gain.

Samsung Bioepis and its R&D subsidiary Epis NexLab signed a research collaboration and license agreement with G2GBio: Samsung Bioepis obtains a full license for a novel long-acting semaglutide asset (GB-7001) plus an option to license a second G2GBio asset, and first-negotiation rights on three further undisclosed candidates. G2GBio will produce and supply the licensed substances; development costs are borne by Samsung Bioepis/Epis NexLab. Samsung Epis Holdings separately invested ₩20 billion in G2GBio convertible bonds.

source.name: BusinessWire (company release, corroborated by Dailypharm/e Today/DigitalToday/etnews)

finding_history.summary: G2GBio presented preclinical InnoLAMP data at ADA 2026, reporting less than 5% initial drug burst within 24 hours and serum concentrations maintained beyond 28 days in rodent models across semaglutide, tirzepatide, and retatrutide, including dual/triple-agonist formulations where high dosing volume typically complicates subcutaneous LAI development. Corroborated by two additional independent outlets covering the same ADA poster.

source.name: Korea Biomedical Review (corroborated by TheBioNews, Asia Business Daily)

finding_history.summary: G2GBio and Boehringer Ingelheim signed a contract expanding their long-acting injectable collaboration to additional peptide formulations via InnoLAMP, building on an initial agreement from January 2025. Not semaglutide-specific — covers unspecified Boehringer peptide candidates.

G2GBio signed an MOU with Celltrion to co-develop an ultra-concentrated antibody subcutaneous injection using a new 'InnoBioLAMP' platform variant — applicable to antibodies, bispecifics, ADCs, and recombinant proteins. Company-level development, not a semaglutide/small-molecule LAI asset; exact announcement date approximate based on 'most recent' framing in source article.
